metadata.description: Comprehensive comparison of 5 approaches for optic disc/cup segmentation
metadata.evaluation_set: Validation set (except CLAHE uses test set)

metrics_description.Loss: Combined CE + Dice loss (lower is better)
metrics_description.IoU BG: Intersection over Union for background class
metrics_description.IoU Disc: Intersection over Union for optic disc class
metrics_description.IoU Cup: Intersection over Union for optic cup class
metrics_description.mIoU: Mean IoU across all three classes (higher is better)
metrics_description.\u0394 mIoU: Improvement/degradation vs Baseline UNet (higher is better)

CLAHE.description: Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization preprocessing

Baseline + Std Enhancer.description: UNet + lightweight encoder-decoder enhancer (52K additional params)

Baseline + Atrous Enhancer.description: UNet + ASPP-based multi-scale enhancer (26K additional params)

ASPP-UNet.description: UNet with ASPP bottleneck for multi-scale features (21.5M total params)

key_findings: ASPP-UNet achieves best performance with 30.9% fewer parameters
Learned enhancement approaches marginally degrade performance
CLAHE preprocessing performs worse than baseline UNet
Architectural multi-scale features outperform preprocessing approaches
Optic cup segmentation remains the most challenging class
